title: Aurelia — source-first mechanical ornithopter
attribution: Stanley J. O. Tinn's photographed notes inform the principles, not the numerical engine, pilot, linkage or aerodynamic specification.

source_readings.readable: Mute swan. Rounded Say full span 7.4 ft, wrist span 3.7 ft = 50% b. Original paragraph: estimated total wing area 6.61 square feet, AR=b²/S about 8.29; elliptical outer wing estimate is compared with 7.83 from another table.
source_readings.used: AR=7.4²/6.61; wrist fraction=3.7/7.4. Broad constant-chord inner panel, rounded tapered outer panels, articulated wrist.
source_readings.uncertain: Handwritten amendments are not reliable numerical specifications. The 3.135 ft wing-length conversion is inconsistent and excluded.
source_readings.completion: Span scaled to 14 m; extended area=196/AR. Four-segment outer ellipse and tip taper are supplied engineering geometry.

source_readings.readable: Göttingen 417a curved plate plot, multiple coefficient axes, curves labelled Re 168000 and Re 42000.
source_readings.used: Distinct illustrative inner airfoil and outer curved-plate polars, and explicit camber dependence.
source_readings.uncertain: Multiple scales, curve identities and exact numeric ordinates are ambiguous; this low-Re plot is not a full-scale coefficient table.
source_readings.completion: Bundled engineering section tables are linearly interpolated with endpoint clamp, camber increments and nominal-AR induced drag; no claimed chart digitisation.

source_readings.readable: Bird flight as a guide to ornithopter design. Define an ideal sine-wave trajectory; cruise speed and flapping frequency define required vertical force range, against which candidate actions may be evaluated. Powered man-carrying aim.
source_readings.used: Comparison is diagnostic only. Free flight follows calculated forces, not the target trajectory; seated adult pilot.
source_readings.uncertain: Appendices and complete underlying design algorithm are absent; marginal historical revision is not a performance specification.
source_readings.completion: 55 kg clothed/helmeted adult, provided world, finite 16 kW motor and explicit dynamical state.

source_readings.readable: Straight and level flapping flight cannot be literally steady: lift/thrust vary cyclically, giving a slightly undulating trajectory and unsteady airspeed. Bounding and ring-gait flight are discussed. Powered man-carrying ornithopter is named.
source_readings.used: Wingbeat-dependent strip forces and real COM translation; no artificially constant altitude or forward thrust.
source_readings.uncertain: Top handwritten sentence is only partly legible; illustrated vortex rings do not supply quantitative wake data.
source_readings.completion: Quasi-steady strips omit explicit wake shedding and ring vortices.

source_readings.readable: Low speed downstroke lasts longer than recovery; periods become equal as speed increases. Wing-wishbone-body assembly can be modelled as a resonant system. Candidate forces should be compared with those needed for the desired trajectory.
source_readings.used: Fixed quick-return bias .3 at low speed or 0 for equal cruise timing; elastic wing/body dynamics; required versus actual force comparison.
source_readings.uncertain: Crossed-out double-parabola argument and heavily revised margins are uncertain; no recovered unique trajectory amplitude.
source_readings.completion: theta=phi-b sin(phi); setting changes require reset. Spring 28000 Nm/rad, reflected inertia and all damping are supplied assumptions.

source_readings.readable: Wing and body inertias plus wishbone springiness form a mass-spring system about common CG. Fore/aft wing movement changes separation of CG and lift centre, producing pitching moment, with tail assistance. Wing action divides arm and hand; working action pulls down/back, recovery trails with feathers closing.
source_readings.used: Coupled phase/pitch mass matrix, CG body reaction, explicit sweep linkage, feathering and sliding-leaf recovery overlap retaining hidden mass.
source_readings.uncertain: No complete quick-return mechanism or structural dimensions are recoverable; marginal changes and missing referenced material remain unresolved.
source_readings.completion: Two rigid half-length outer leaves; sinusoidal linkage curves; actual distributed geometry and numerical phase derivatives from supplied helper.

source_readings.readable: Opening continuation says reduced area and span on recovery, repeated cycle, with local incidence adjustment; handwritten addition mentions camber. Goshawk example has different wing proportions and listed cambers 13%, 10%, 9%, 6%.
source_readings.used: Camber, incidence/twist and thickness remain separate. Recovery overlap reduces exposed area/span. Curved production surfaces change with camber.
source_readings.uncertain: Goshawk percentages are not swan measurements and are not transferred to this aircraft.
source_readings.completion: Inner/outer base camber .022/.045 with .008/.015 cyclic increments, independently of twist; all supplied illustrative engineering assumptions.

source_readings.readable: Inner arm thickness 5–6%; outer hand effectively a thin slotted curved plate. Local force directions must be evaluated from steep tip trajectory. Partial closing cuts recovery area/drag. Conventional tail or weight shift appropriate; fin/rudder advantageous. Swan running takeoff and increased takeoff frequency discussed.
source_readings.used: 5.5% inner structural metadata, thin .8% outer leaves, local relative-flow lift/drag, conventional stabiliser/elevator and fin/rudder, wheeled runway takeoff.
source_readings.uncertain: Animal takeoff angles and approximate frequency/stiffness changes are contextual, not a mechanical aircraft operating schedule.
source_readings.completion: Fixed supplied amplitudes and finite-power governor; no automatic frequency change. Three-wheel reduced contact, tail area/arm/incidence, finite pilot controls are engineering additions.

source_readings.readable: Baseline glide power Dg V /550 horsepower with Dg=W/(L/D). Further power terms include extra induced drag, horizontal acceleration, lifting through the cycle and wing inertia; inertial requirement vanishes without damping. Man-carrying powered application and missing design appendix are noted.
source_readings.used: Local drag work, coupled kinetic energy and hinge spring energy, finite shaft input, transmission/damping heat and fuel accounting. Spring exchanges energy but supplies no net propulsive work.
source_readings.uncertain: Appendix 12 and complete revisions are unavailable. Marginal dimensional note is not adopted as an aircraft coefficient.
source_readings.completion: 85% transmission, BSFC .55 kg/kWh, idle fuel, finite starting torque and supplied frozen glide equilibrium; no biological/metabolic efficiency substituted for shaft efficiency.

engineering_completion.mass_allocations: Unmodified supplied engineering mass_budget, including all 30 kg of wings through overlap.
engineering_completion.construction: Conceptual composite-tube triangulated frame, alloy fittings, bronze-coloured bearings and root spring cartridges, cream technical fabric, overlapping grey outer leaves, exposed reduction stage, fuel tank, air-cooled motor, restrained seated pilot and conventional red control surfaces.
engineering_completion.passive_stability: Supplied 1000 Nm s/rad pitch damping is dissipative, not an attitude controller. Neutral pilot supplies zero pitch torque.
engineering_completion.contact: Reduced all-gear constraint at body pitch zero; Ag includes CG vertical-motion inertia and normal load tests release. Torus tyres rotate about lateral z axles. Touchdown sink subtracts body-relative CG motion.
engineering_completion.integration: Midpoint RK2 with substeps at most 1/240 s, actual coupled acceleration, work and fuel at the midpoint.
engineering_completion.glide: Frozen extended wing preset only while gliding=true. Host handles explicit pilot clutch release. Zero-throttle powered mechanism coasts rather than resetting.

limitations: Educational favourable reduction, not a recovered buildable design, structural substantiation or validated human-flight prediction.
Engine continuous rating/derating, BSFC, large reflected drive inertia, full-scale section coefficients and passive damping are assumptions, not Stanley's notebook measurements.
No local section pitching moments, wake dynamics, overlap interference, flexible structure, aerodynamic hysteresis or roll/yaw inertia coupling.
Tail shape and construction detail are visual engineering interpretations; masses and forces follow the declared reduced representation rather than a structural finite-element model.
Reduced three-wheel contact has no suspension dynamics. Rolling and braking dissipate energy; impacts are not an elastic bounce model.
Missing appendices, section measurements and uncertain handwritten revisions remain missing.
No execution, tests, syntax checks or rendered previews were performed under the file-only policy.
